verdicts.strongest_argument: This is reachable-but-unconnected and I keep it in that band, but with a caveat that cuts harder here than at any other name on this day. The 8-K is in filings.json with an item code and a date, so it was public three weeks before the print; the body is not stored, so nobody - hunter or adversary - knows what it says, and a finding whose content is unknown cannot carry a sign. The hunter concedes that. The caveat is the coverage asymmetry: LULU is one of only four tickers in this whole capture that carries real news items, and the capture ran a 22-query news sweep on the morning of the print plus a 150-item first sweep, and neither surfaced any August company announcement. For a $12.5bn household-name consumer stock, that is weak but genuine evidence of immateriality rather than of a missed disclosure - a material standalone 8-K at this company would be reported, unlike at the twenty-nine names in this run where n_queries=0 makes silence uninformative. Item 8.01 is also the catch-all used for entirely routine things: setting an earnings date, a debt or buyback authorisation, an investor-day notice, a legal-proceedings update with no financial effect. The 13D/A bracketing adds nothing without a holder name or a stake size, both absent.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The proxy contest, its resolution and the CEO succession are all published, and the finding half-admits it ('the proxy fight was covered'). A PREC14A is mailed to every holder; a DEFA14A of 2026-06-05 is in filings.json; an 8-K carrying item 5.07 on 2026-06-26 is the certified record of the vote, publicly filed; and the leadership half - Calvin McDonald's departure announced on the December 2025 call and Heidi O'Neill's appointment being read as a vote of no confidence - is in the captured coverage (tradingkey piece, cited in the brief's own independence field, and docs/a6714b8a9efb77fcb23338c7664926c08439b598.txt from snapshots/20260903T151408Z.json item 19). A founder-led proxy campaign at a company of this profile is among the most covered governance events of the year; the notion that its outcome went unreported is not credible and the finding's evidence for it is the absence of a headline in a 22-query sweep. I also think the filing pattern is misread. Two Form 3s and eleven Form 4s all dated 2026-06-29, three days after an annual meeting, is the ordinary annual-meeting mechanic: directors receive their annual equity grant immediately after the AGM, which produces a Form 4 for every continuing director, while a Form 3 is filed only by genuinely new insiders. Eleven Form 4s therefore indicate eleven existing insiders being granted, not eleven new ones seated - the count of new arrivals is two. That materially weakens 'a reconstituted board'. What remains is the kitchen-sink heuristic - new board plus new CEO equals reset quarter - which is generic, unsized and undated, and its sign is not even stable, since a reset can clear the decks and be bought.
